subject: Expressing x-axis intervals with the gray space in the facet strips

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Expressing x-axis intervals with the gray space in the facet strips
parts:
Hello ggploters,

I was wondering if it was possible to customize the strip on a facet
so that it can provide a little information about the x-axis. I have
been using geom_rect to make rectangles within the plotting area like
so:

## data generation
library(ggplot2)
x <-runif(80, 1,8)
data <- as.data.frame(x)
data$y <--runif(80, 0, 125)
data$z <- factor(c("A","A","B","B"))

## data frame to determine bounds of the rectangles
data_annot <- data.frame(left=c(1,3,5), right=c(3,5,8),
label=c("Left","Mid","Right"))

## actual plot
ggplot(data) +
geom_rect(data=data_annot, aes(xmin=left, xmax=right, fill=label,
ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf), alpha=0.2) +
geom_line(aes(x,y), colour="gray80") +
scale_fill_brewer(palette="Greys") +
facet_wrap(~z, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
theme_bw()

Now this plot is fine in colour but when I want to produce a black and
white plot -like above- things get a little muddled in all that gray.
I was wondering if it was possible to achieve the same effect
(rectangles corresponding to intervals on the x-axis) using the gray
space in the facet strip? It isn't apparent to me how to do this
looking at the facet documentation so I thought I would ask to see if
anyone else has ever tried to achieve this result.

Thanks in advance!

Sam
